title: Rectangle Totals in a Fixed Grid
statement:
Build a helper that answers many "what is the total inside this rectangle?" questions about one grid of numbers that never changes.

  • GridTotals(grid) stores the grid.
  • regionTotal(r1, c1, r2, c2) returns the sum of every cell grid[r][c] with r1 ≤ r ≤ r2 and c1 ≤ c ≤ c2. (r1, c1) is the top-left corner and (r2, c2) the bottom-right; both are included.

Each query must run in O(1).

Tests are a list of operations and their arguments; the first operation creates the object. The expected output has one entry per operation (null for the constructor).

examples.why: A rectangle can be a single cell.

constraints: 0 ≤ r1 ≤ r2 < rows, 0 ≤ c1 ≤ c2 < cols
hints: In one dimension, a range total is the difference of two prefix totals. What is the 2D version of a prefix?
Let P[r][c] be the total of the rectangle from the top-left corner to just before (r, c). It can be filled from its top, left and top-left neighbours.
A query rectangle is the big corner rectangle minus the strip above it, minus the strip to its left, plus the top-left block you subtracted twice.

explain.intuition:
Store P[r][c] = the total of all cells above and to the left of (r, c), using one extra row and column of zeros so the edges need no special cases. Building it is inclusion–exclusion: P[r+1][c+1] = grid[r][c] + P[r][c+1] + P[r+1][c] − P[r][c], because the top-left block was counted in both neighbours.

A query uses the same idea backwards. Take the corner rectangle ending at (r2, c2), cut off the rows above r1 and the columns left of c1, and add back the top-left corner that was cut twice. Four lookups, no matter how big the rectangle. Image tools use this same table, called a summed-area table, to blur regions quickly.
steps: For each cell, set P[r+1][c+1] = grid[r][c] + P[r][c+1] + P[r+1][c] − P[r][c].
For a query, return P[r2+1][c2+1] − P[r1][c2+1] − P[r2+1][c1] + P[r1][c1].
pitfalls: Forgetting to add back the top-left block. It is removed once by each of the two subtractions.
Mixing the +1 offsets. With a zero row and column in front, every query index on the far side gets +1 and every near-side index does not.
Building one prefix array per row only. Queries then cost O(rows), not O(1).

complexity.time: O(rows · cols) to build, O(1) per query

solutions.title: Add up the rectangle each time
solutions.idea: Loop over every cell of the rectangle on each query.

solutions.title: 2D prefix sums
solutions.idea: Precompute corner totals once; each query combines four of them with inclusion–exclusion.
solutions.time: O(rows · cols) build, O(1) per query

followups: Cells can now change between queries. What structure supports both updates and rectangle totals in O(log² n)?
